### OSIQ: drop potentially overlapping items and compute modified mean scores
osiq_drop_items <- c("osiq_o_22", "osiq_o_28")

df_master <-
  df_master %>%
  ### calculate OSIQ-O & OSIQ-S difference score (+ve = more O, -ve = more S)
  mutate(osiq_diff_o_s = osiq_o - osiq_s) %>%
  ### calculate OSIQ-O without items 22 and 28
  mutate(
    osiq_o_drop = rowMeans(
      select(
        ### mean of all OSIQ-O items, without the items labelled in `osiq_drop_items`
        ### (raw responses are the variables ending in digits; luckily, 27r is spatial so it can be ignored)
        ., starts_with("osiq_o_") & matches('\\d{1}$') & !matches(osiq_drop_items)
        )
      )
    ) 

### IES-R: drop potentially overlapping items and recompute scores
ies_drop_items <- c("ies_recent_9", "ies_remote_9")

### identify items in the regular ies-r intrusions subscale
ies_int <- c("_1", "_2", "_3", "_6", "_9", "_14", "_16", "_20")

df_master <-
  df_master %>%
  ### calculate ies-r recent without item 9
  mutate(
    ### total sum score
    ies_recent_total_drop = rowSums(
      select(
        ., starts_with("ies_recent_") & matches('\\d{1}$') & !matches(ies_drop_items) & !contains("cutoff")
        )
      ),
    ### int domain mean score
    ies_recent_int_drop = rowMeans(
      select(
        ., starts_with("ies_recent_") & matches('\\d{1}$') & !matches(ies_drop_items) & ends_with(ies_int)
        )
      )
    ) %>% 
  ### calculate ies-r remote without item 9
  mutate(
    ### total sum score
    ies_remote_total_drop = rowSums(
      select(
        ., starts_with("ies_remote_") & matches('\\d{1}$') & !matches(ies_drop_items) & !contains("cutoff")
        )
      ),
    ### int domain mean score
    ies_remote_int_drop = rowMeans(
      select(
        ., starts_with("ies_remote_") & matches('\\d{1}$') & !matches(ies_drop_items) & ends_with(ies_int)
        )
      )
    )

### Center numeric predictors used in later models

  mutate(
    ### osiq_o

    ### osiq_s

    ### phq_total

    ### osiq diff score
    osiq_diff_o_s_cen = scale(osiq_diff_o_s, scale = FALSE),
    ### age
    age_flup_cen = scale(age_flup, scale = FALSE),
    ### pte_exposure_count
    pte_exposure_count_cen = scale(pte_exposure_count, scale = FALSE),
    ### grammatical reasoning
    final_score_raw_gr_cen = scale(final_score_raw_gr, scale = FALSE),
    ### odd-one-out
    final_score_raw_oo_cen = scale(final_score_raw_oo, scale = FALSE),
    ### paired associates
    avg_score_raw_pa_cen = scale(avg_score_raw_pa, scale = FALSE),
    ### mental rotation
    final_score_raw_ro_cen = scale(final_score_raw_ro, scale = FALSE),
    ### education

    )

### Define the analysis dataset for comparing the two dependent correlations

As in Study 1, the OSIVQ verbal scale (Blazhenkova & Kozhevnikov, 2009) was administered but did not affect interpretation (see the Supplemental Material).

The verbal scale of the OSIVQ (Blazhenkova & Kozhevnikov, 2009) has been proposed as a measure of verbal-semantic processes, which are also thought to be protective against intrusions (Holmes & Bourne, 2008). Although we administered this verbal scale in both studies, it was not consistently related to PTSD symptoms: Although higher verbal-cognitive style was related to fewer symp- toms in Study 1, this effect was restricted to men and did not replicate in Study 2. Furthermore, its inclusion in regression models had negligible effects on our other findings, suggesting that the visual and spatial-schematic domains may be particularly relevant to PTSD symp- toms (see the Supplemental Material).
